groups.name: BirdLife International
groups.blurb: The global partnership of national bird conservation societies. Its partner directory points you to the society in almost any country.

groups.name: eBird
groups.blurb: The worldwide platform for logging what you see. Your lists feed real science and connect you to birders near you.

groups.name: Global Big Day
groups.blurb: One day each May when tens of thousands of birders in almost every country count together. Anyone can join with a single checklist.

groups.name: October Big Day
groups.blurb: The autumn counterpart to Global Big Day, held each October to catch the southbound migration. Free to join from anywhere.

groups.name: iNaturalist
groups.blurb: A worldwide naturalist community where members help identify each other's photos and sound recordings.

groups.name: Observation.org
groups.blurb: International sightings platform used across Europe, Africa and beyond, with the ObsIdentify app.

groups.name: Xeno-canto
groups.blurb: A global community sharing and identifying bird sound recordings from every continent.

groups.name: Motus Wildlife Tracking System
groups.blurb: An international network of receiving stations tracking tagged birds. Volunteers host and monitor stations.

groups.name: World Migratory Bird Day
groups.blurb: A global campaign with public events, walks and counts on two days each year across all flyways.

groups.name: Global Birdfair
groups.blurb: The largest annual gathering of birders, clubs and conservation projects from around the world.

groups.name: r/birding on Reddit
groups.blurb: A large open forum for birders everywhere to share sightings, questions and trip reports.

groups.name: r/whatsthisbird on Reddit
groups.blurb: Post a photo from anywhere in the world and experienced birders will help you identify it.

groups.name: Feminist Bird Club
groups.blurb: Chapters on several continents run free, inclusive bird walks open to anyone.

groups.name: Birdability
groups.blurb: The community for birders with disabilities and other health concerns, with an accessible sites map anyone can add to.

groups.name: Black AF In STEM and Black Birders Week
groups.blurb: The collective behind Black Birders Week, a worldwide programme of talks, walks and online events.

groups.name: Female Bird Day and the Galbatross Project
groups.blurb: A yearly global challenge to notice and record the overlooked female half of every species.

groups.name: Global Young Birders Network
groups.blurb: Connects birders under 25 worldwide to young birder clubs, camps and careers with birds.

groups.name: African Bird Club
groups.blurb: The society for birders across Africa, with country checklists, a journal and conservation grants.

groups.name: Oriental Bird Club
groups.blurb: Covers birders and birds across South and South East Asia, with an image database and grants.

groups.name: Neotropical Bird Club
groups.blurb: The club for Central and South America and the Caribbean, publishing Cotinga and Neotropical Birding.

groups.name: OSME
groups.blurb: The Ornithological Society of the Middle East, the Caucasus and Central Asia, with the journal Sandgrouse.

groups.name: BirdsCaribbean
groups.blurb: The regional network for the Caribbean islands, running the Caribbean Waterbird Census and festivals.

groups.name: European Bird Census Council
groups.blurb: Links the national monitoring schemes behind the European Breeding Bird Atlas.

groups.name: International Wader Study Group
groups.blurb: A worldwide network of amateurs and scientists studying waders and shorebirds.

groups.name: Wader Quest
groups.blurb: A small international charity and community of shorebird enthusiasts supporting local conservation projects.

groups.name: The Waterbird Society
groups.blurb: An international society for anyone interested in waterbird study and conservation.

groups.name: World Seabird Union
groups.blurb: Brings together seabird groups from every ocean, with a worldwide conference every few years.

groups.name: Raptor Research Foundation
groups.blurb: The global society for people who study and watch birds of prey.

groups.name: Wetlands International
groups.blurb: Runs the International Waterbird Census, the world's largest volunteer waterbird count.

groups.name: Spring Alive
groups.blurb: A BirdLife project for children and families across Europe, Africa and Asia to record the first migrants of spring.
